what_it_does: Sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) — multiplying a large table of numbers where most entries are zero by a vector — is a fundamental operation in scientific computing, graph analytics, and some AI workloads. The challenge is that the pattern of non-zero entries varies wildly by problem, causing irregular, hard-to-predict memory access patterns that leave hardware largely idle. SPASM is a combined software-and-hardware approach: the software side analyzes an input matrix, identifies recurring local patterns of non-zero locations, and groups them into a portfolio of compact templates. The hardware side is a reconfigurable computing structure that can switch between those templates at runtime, tile by tile, keeping the memory and arithmetic units busy regardless of the matrix's overall structure. A scheduling step assigns tiles to computing units to keep the load balanced.
